_comment: Populous bench SCENE DEFINITION (201F4F51 template-free). Same form as ClickTrainer/SolarBirth: a behaviour + a tree of primitive component KINDS + exits, authored as data. The bench owns + loads its own scene file (the shell manifest is for shell scenes); populous.lua orchestrates + the globe draws in the rtt pane. Retires the invented populous.tree.json (1F151933).

children._comment: One tab rail PER PAGE, each gated on its page's arrange() key and all binding the one `tab` value — the catalog's ratified per-page PTT pattern. An unplaced rail neither draws nor steps, so the shared step names never double-fire.

populous_globe._comment: The POPULOUS hex ledger globe — the authored world drawn into the multi-view's centre viewport. It deliberately has NO `camera` block: the map is flown by the game master, so the scene's own orbit camera owns the view and the stage authors only the light it is seen by (the default light source). `clear` is transparent so the node's holder panel shows through. This world has NO simulation publishing shells, so its whole appearance is authored here: the near-black under-shell, the inset tile shell over it (the seams between the tiles show the shell beneath, and those seams ARE the outlines — two static shells, no per-edge line geometry), and the shared reference frame above both.
populous_globe._hdr: HDR: the `scene` pass (the globe's two shells + graticule, the layers above) renders into the LINEAR rgba16f `hdr` working attachment and `tonemap_grade` resolves it (ACES roll-off) into the sRGB `color` last. grade_strength 0 = tonemap only, no invented tint — an art grade is Aaron's to author in-window. Alpha passes through, so the transparent clear the holder panel shows through survives.

populous_hex._comment: The HEX-STACK inspector — one column of the world, up close. Authors NO shell layers and no graticule: the column is published data (the scene's own shells), alone under the stage's light; the camera is the scene's orbit, aimed at the stack. Same HDR resolve as the globe so the heat ramp reads identically in both panes.

load._comment: The bootstrap-roll progress bar reuses the loading-screen gauge look (same values as Loading.scene.json load.gauge); per-scene styles by design, palette tokens single-sourced in ui_theme.json.

rtt_holder._comment: The framed RTT HOLDER every bench's rtt/viewport slot styles against — the shared chrome for an offscreen-view slot (replaced the per-scene assetpipeline holder block, same values).
